_comment: EWL-FOLD BENEFIT, corrected design.  The first attempt (runs/golden_0729/ewlfold) was
INERT: uwl_dual_top=true (from the all-on delta) makes the loader FORCE ewl_fold_rows
=false — 'a cycle decided by both the preferred and the fallback rung must never fold two
integer rows (the F-A refold class)', GnssConfigLoadNetwork.cpp:2651.  It warned; I missed it.
So both arms here drop to the PLAIN SINGLE-TOP lane tier:
uwl_dual_top   false  (else the fold is forced off)
uwl_mid_enable false  (the E6 mid hop is ALSO doubly-decided but has NO refold guard —
only dual_top does; folding with it on would double-count unguarded)
uwl_sib_gate   false  (documented INERT without dual_top — don't arm dead knobs)
Lanes remaining, each decided ONCE: GPS EWL (L2,L5) lam 5.861 m + Galileo UWL (E5b,E5a)
lam 9.768 m.  mw_wl.enable stays FALSE (WL-1 float layer is measured net-harmful).
The two arms differ in exactly ONE functional key: mw_wl.ewl_fold_rows.
PRIMARY metric: network_sh_spectrum.csv ev1..ev5 + mass_pb/span_pb (does folding the
near-perfect EWL integers lift the ~0.139 soft-end plateau that 22 third-band phase-bias
states sit on?).  SECONDARY: the known churn cost from network_epoch_status.csv.
